handbookNote: Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, AAMVA base content Version: July 2017, Minnesota-specific front matter Form Number PS30002-33, 01/2022), published by the Minnesota Department of Public Safety (DPS), Division of Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) -- fetched directly from https://assets.dps.mn.gov/files/dvs/Commercial-Drivers-License-Manual.pdf on 2026-08-22 (7.6MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/mn_cdl_research/mn_cdl_manual_full.txt, 11,547 lines). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: neither the Minnesota-specific Part A front matter (Commercial Driver's License Tests section) nor any AAMVA base-manual text in this document states an exact knowledge-test item count or a number-correct-to-pass for any Minnesota CDL knowledge test (general knowledge or any endorsement) -- the manual describes which knowledge tests are required for which class/endorsement combination (via its Figure 1.2 'What to Study' chart) but never discloses question counts or a passing threshold, and the only explicit '80%' figure anywhere in the source text applies to the separate federal Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) theory-training assessment, not the CDL knowledge test itself. Several third-party test-prep sites converge on '50 questions, 40 correct (80%) to pass' for Minnesota's general knowledge test, but this could not be confirmed on any official mn.gov or dps.mn.gov source and is therefore NOT asserted as fact in this question bank -- per this project's no-default-values discipline this is explicitly hedged rather than borrowed from another state or an unverified third party, consistent with the AL/AR/KS/IN/ME/MD precedent. What IS confirmed directly from the official Minnesota manual: the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score applies regardless (49 CFR 383.135(a), same as every other CDL-track state in this project); Minnesota's three CDL classes are A (any vehicle towing a unit of more than 10,000 lbs GVWR with a GCWR over 26,000 lbs), B (a single-unit vehicle over 26,000 lbs GVWR, or one towing a unit of 10,000 lbs GVWR or less), and C (a single-unit vehicle of 26,000 lbs GVWR or less carrying a hazardous materials, passenger, or school-bus-with-passenger endorsement); Minnesota's six CDL endorsement codes are H (Hazardous Materials), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger Transport), S (School Bus), T (Doubles/Triples), and X (Tanker + Hazardous Materials combined); Minnesota's restriction-code table is unusually granular at eleven codes (E, K, L, M, N, O, P, V, W, X, Z), notably including a state-specific 'W - Buses less than 24 passenger capacity' code not found in every other state's manual; a Minnesota commercial learner's permit (CLP) is valid 180 days and may be renewed but never for more than one year total from initial issuance, and must be held at least 14 calendar days before the CDL skills test may be attempted; the CDL Skills Test has three ordered phases (vehicle inspection, basic control skills, road test), each of which must be passed before advancing to the next; a 'No Show' examination fee (Minnesota Statutes section 171.13) has applied since Nov. 1, 2021 for missed or late-cancelled skills-test appointments; Minnesota exempts several state-specific driver categories from CDL licensing entirely, including authorized emergency-vehicle drivers, qualifying farm-truck drivers operating within 150 miles of the farm, personal-use recreational-vehicle drivers, and -- notably unusual among CDL-track states in this project -- backup snowplow drivers employed by a local government of 3,000 or fewer residents who hold a Class D license and are temporarily covering for the regular snowplow operator during a snow emergency; the tank/hazmat endorsement volume thresholds (individual tank capacity over 119 gallons, aggregate capacity 1,000+ gallons) match the federal standard incorporated into the manual. Content-depth rationale: Minnesota uses the same AAMVA-authored 'Modernized Testing System' base manual (Version: July 2017) as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Massachusetts), organized into the same 13 core AAMVA sections -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split here into three buckets for volume: 02_driving_safely_a covering vehicle inspection/basic control/shifting/seeing/communicating/speed/space management through subsection 2.7, 02b_seeing_hazards_distraction covering the seeing-hazards and distracted-driving subsections 2.8-2.9, and 03_driving_safely_b covering night/extreme-condition driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, emergency maneuvers, ABS, skid control, accident/fire procedures, and alcohol/drugs), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets), Section 10 School Buses (generic AAMVA content), Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving (12 and 13 combined into one bucket) -- PLUS Minnesota-specific Part A front matter (CDL classes, endorsements/restrictions, exemptions, tests overview, medical requirements, general information, and Minnesota Trucking Regulations, layered into the licensing bucket alongside AAMVA Section 1's federal disqualification/self-certification/IRP-IFTA material) and a notably rich, wholly Minnesota-specific 'Part B: Minnesota School Bus Driver's Handbook' (nearly 1,000 lines of state-specific school-bus licensing, certification, danger-zone, and procedural content, distinct from and supplementary to the generic AAMVA Section 10 School Buses content) that this project gave its own dedicated bucket (12b_mn_school_bus_handbook) rather than folding into or displacing the generic AAMVA school-bus bucket (12_school_bus_aamva) -- this Part B handbook is unusually extensive compared to most other states built so far and was sized up accordingly rather than compressed. Some sections (Cargo, Doubles/Triples, Tank Vehicles) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Minnesota manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
